Episode 251: The Great Adversaries (8)
Jin looked at Syris in surprise.
She wore her usual expressionless face, appearing detached from everything and indifferent to everyone. However, as a long-time colleague and friend, Jin knew why Syris always wore that expression.
Responsibility.
From the moment she became aware of who she was, Syris's life had been filled with training to become the perfect future leader of the Ice Castle.
A harsh and tedious life.
Syris had been accustomed to such a life from a very young age. She never thought that anything else could interfere with her life dedicated to the Ice Castle.
That was until she met Jin.
Chatter...
Syris filled their glasses with wine.
"The day we first met, you tricked me in Mamit. Haha... Now that I think about it, it was strange that I even applied the ointment for you."
"In what way?"

"At first, I just handed you the ointment to apply yourself. But then, after seeing your dirty hands, I decided to apply it for you. Normally, I wouldn’t have even given you the ointment, let alone apply it myself."
"That's true."

"It was just strange to meet someone my age in such a rough place. From a young age, I often acted on behalf of my mother, and when I left the Ice Castle, it was usually for missions. I hardly ever had conversations with peers."
Jin nodded, recalling Talaris. She often boasted about sending Syris to important meetings in her place from when Syris was about five years old while she went to meet her lovers.
Of course, this was to boast about how smart Syris was, but it also highlighted the immense pressure Syris faced growing up as the heir of the Ice Castle. In essence, she
received emperor training every moment and was constantly tested.
"So, when I rescued you and found out you were the youngest of the Runkandels... I was really furious. But after some time, I realized I wasn't angry at you."
"....Angry at yourself for being deceived?"
"Right. I was angry at myself. For foolishly showing a small kindness and making a mockery of the Ice Castle... And I even lost the duel. That's what I thought."
Swoop...
Syris downed her wine in one gulp and smiled. Jin followed suit and refilled their glasses.

"But after losing and applying ointment to you again... amidst feelings of defeat and disappointment, I strangely felt refreshed. You know what I'm trying to say? Actually, I always wanted to escape the pressure. The pressure of being the heir of the Ice Castle."
Despite their long time together...
Jin was hearing these inner thoughts of Syris for the first time. He had never noticed them before. She had always been the perfect heir of the Ice Castle.
From around the time she turned fifteen, those under the protection of the Ice Castle sought Syris instead of Talaris when problems arose.

"I had no choice but to work hard, Jin. I am less talented than my mother. She was among the top three warriors of her time, even while living playfully... I’ve never missed a day of training, yet I'm not even among the top five of this generation. That's why my mother was so harsh on me from a young age."
Jin didn't respond but simply clinked his glass lightly with hers.
"For me, you were always a good rival. Our relationship started unexpectedly, and the experiences we shared were dangerous but mystical. How many times did you owe your life to our Ice Castle?"
"Countless times."
From Colon onwards, the Ice Castle had always generously supported Jin. Even when coming to Mila to meet the people of the Demon World, he rode Mott.
"I've received so much help from you, Syris. No matter what I do, I could never fully repay it."
"Yes, you should be aware if you have a conscience. Haha, now braid my hair."
"Braid your hair?"
"Never tried it?"
"I don't think so."
Syris demonstrated by pulling her long hair over her shoulder and showing how to braid it.
"Put the hair strands between your fingers, gently tie them like a knot... like this. Here, and up to here, just braid three strands."
"I'll try to make it as pretty as possible."
"Good, if it's not pretty, I'll turn my chin away."
Jin stood up and positioned himself behind Syris. As he combed and flipped her hair, a sweet scent filled the air.
Jin concentrated and didn't speak first, while Syris started humming softly at some point.
One strand was completely braided.
When Jin held the mirror to show her the finished braid, their eyes met in the reflection. They both couldn't help but smile.
"How is it? I tried my best."
"Hmm, good. Please finish the rest."
Jin resumed braiding, and Syris continued humming.
Jin thought, for the first time in a long while, or perhaps for the first time ever, he was witnessing Syris showing a light-hearted side.
She was beautiful. Her silver-white hair shimmered like sunlight dancing on a river.
"There was a time."
"Yes, Syris."
"A time when I thought the same as my mother."
"What do you mean...?"

"One day, it occurred to me that bringing you in as the master of the Ice Castle might actually be a good idea. I don't remember exactly when. Was it during the retrieval of the compass? Anyway, it seemed like the best thing for the Ice Castle."
For the Ice Castle.
Syris mulled over these words as she took another sip of her wine.
"You might not understand, but this issue was a long-standing dilemma for me. I couldn't tell whether I wanted to marry you just for the sake of the Ice Castle, or if it was because I loved you."
Jin couldn't respond.
But Syris wasn't bothered by his silence. After all, she hadn't started this conversation expecting any answers.
"It had to be the former. I wanted to marry you, not because I loved you, but solely for the sake of the Ice Castle."
Jin's hands slightly trembled as he continued braiding her hair, which Syris found oddly satisfying. She playfully asked a question, spurred by a sudden whimsy.
"Jin, why don't you ask if your opinion isn't important?"
"That's not..."
"You could have just refused, right?"
"It's not like that."
"Haha, of course it's not. You would have refused. You already had someone in your heart, after all."
Valeria Hister.

Syris knew about the night Jin and Valeria had spent together in the Red Owl. As soon as she heard the news, she decided it was time to talk to Jin. Just once, she wanted to share her feelings with him.
"Jin."
"Yes."
"Regrettably, from my perspective... at some point, it wasn't just for the Ice Castle... I found myself cherishing you. I respected you as a rival, liked you as a friend, and loved you as a man."
The second strand of hair was now braided. Jin steadied his trembling hands and began on the last strand.
"Why are you shaking? I'm the one who confessed. I won’t let it slide if you mess up the braid."
"Syris..."

"It would have been better if I realized these feelings earlier. And if I had been more expressive like my mother... maybe there could have been a chance. But now, it's time to close this chapter of my heart. For the Ice Castle, and for all of us."
All of us.
Syris used that term, not just for Jin and herself, but for all their comrades.
"The battles ahead will be harder than any we've faced. I don't want to make mistakes. I've already made my choice."
Jin couldn't find the words to reply.
He simply continued braiding her hair, the trembling in his hands finally subsiding. When he finished the last braid, Jin showed her the reflection in the mirror.
"Oh, you did a meticulous job till the end."
And just as Jin was about to nod in agreement.
Syris, turning around, naturally pulled his neck towards her and their lips met.
"This settles all the debts you owe the Ice Castle as a rival. From now on, there will be no debts between us."
To me, you're the closest friend and the most precious person.
"So, feel free to ask for anything you need in the future. Just be as brazen as you are now. Got it? But, promise me two things."
"...What are they?"
"First, I hope the way you treat me doesn't change. I've grown more comfortable with you than before. Can you do that?"
Jin slowly nodded.
"Second... This might make me sound bad, but whatever. It's unlikely anyway. If you ever feel that your feelings for Valeria are not everlasting, come to me."
Syris then turned away.
She didn't want to see the moisture in Jin's eyes or hear his response to the second promise.
Not because she expected him to shake his head. It was out of respect for Valeria, their equally precious comrade.
Two glasses, one glass of wine remaining.
Syris filled her glass with the remaining wine. Just as she was about to drink it, she impulsively created a chill.
Whooosh...
The wine glass, filled with frosty coldness, instantly froze, resembling a blooming snowflower.
"...Somehow, I don't feel like drinking this now. I'll come back when I think of it again. Let's go, Jin. You go ahead and wait for me, I'll ask the manager to keep this and then follow."
After Jin left, Syris stared at the frozen glass for a while.
It was the heart of the heir of the Ice Castle.
